skills.name: using-devia
skills.trigger: Start of every conversation: how the method's skills work and when to load them.
skills.note: Replaces the bootstrap skill of the library Devia Method started from. Keeps the rule (load a skill if there is even a small chance it applies) and the red flags; drops the per-harness tool-mapping references; adds the skill index and the map of Devia's surfaces. Anything new is never the trivial exception.

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.trigger: Before building or changing anything non-trivial: find out what the user really wants, agree a design, record it as a kanban spec.
skills.note: Keeps the conversation (one question at a time, playback, approaches, sizing, hard gate). Recalls memory and existing specs before asking; the design IS a kanban spec (no docs/ file, no commit); approval by card; decisions go to memory; a spike gets its own pane. Visual companion and its server removed.

skills.name: writing-plans
skills.trigger: A design is agreed and the work has several steps: write the plan as kanban tasks.
skills.note: The plan is kanban tasks (dependsOn orders them); the plan header goes into the spec description and each task body keeps upstream's task structure (files, interfaces, TDD steps with Expected output). Handoff is the plan-approval card, not a file link.

skills.name: executing-plans
skills.trigger: Executing the kanban plan yourself, task by task, with TDD and one final review.
skills.note: Rewritten on the kanban: the task body is the brief, the task thread is the ledger (rulings, deferred minors), closing a task with its commit is the completion record, resuming is kanban_list + git log. The plan file, ledger file, workspace and task-start/task-done scripts are gone. Keeps continuous execution, rulings-not-stalls, the four stops, the completion contract and the final review.

skills.name: subagent-driven-development
skills.trigger: Executing the kanban plan with a fresh subagent per task and a review after each.
skills.note: Same kanban-native bookkeeping as executing-plans, plus kanban_record_subagent for every dispatch. Templates and the fix loop are kept with plan-file references replaced by task ids; the model-selection rules are stated without assuming the controller can pick a model. review-package takes a commit range only; task-verify replaces task-done (runs the tests, never records). resuming.md, sdd-workspace and task-brief are gone.

skills.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skills.trigger: Two or more independent problems that can be worked on at the same time.
skills.note: Adds Devia's split panes (up to four, each with its own worktree) as real parallelism, and states that the agent's own subagent tool is used when it has one.

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.trigger: Work is done or a task is closed: get it reviewed before it goes further.
skills.note: Adds the human review (the review card and the Changes view with line comments) next to the reviewer subagent; requirements come from the kanban task, not a docs/ plan. The reviewer inspects other revisions with git show instead of creating a worktree.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.trigger: Review feedback arrived: verify it technically before acting on it.

skills.name: isolating-work
skills.trigger: Before implementation that should not touch the user's current checkout.
skills.note: Replaces using-git-worktrees. Devia's split panes are the isolation (a worktree and a session branch per pane, managed by Devia). Keeps the detection of an existing isolated workspace; removes manual worktree creation, .worktrees/ and gitignore handling.

skills.name: finishing-work
skills.trigger: Implementation is done and green: verify, hand it to the user, close the loop.
skills.note: Replaces finishing-a-development-branch. Verify, commit, ask for review, then let the user choose by card (leave it ready / push / pull request); close the tasks with their commit, suggest archiving the spec, write the session summary. Removes the local merge, branch deletion and worktree removal — upstream's cleanup deletes anything under worktrees/, which is where Devia keeps its session worktrees.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.trigger: Implementing any feature or bug fix: write the failing test first.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.trigger: Any bug, failing test or unexpected behaviour: find the root cause before fixing.
skills.note: Unchanged discipline. Cross-references lose their namespace prefix, and a fixed bug with a root cause is saved to memory as a bugfix.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.trigger: About to say that something is done, fixed or passing: run the check and read its output first.
skills.note: Unchanged discipline. The evidence goes into the task's closing comment and the step in the progress list.

skills.name: writing-skills
skills.trigger: Creating or editing a skill for Devia, and checking that it changes behaviour.
skills.note: Points at where Devia keeps skills (the Skills manager, .agents/skills and .claude/skills) instead of Claude plugin paths and per-runtime tool-mapping references. The Claude-specific best-practice dump and the CLAUDE.md testing notes are dropped.
